solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrest follows section in plane which has cracks in?

indicators.note: one thing set inside another sits within its outer shell
to follow is to come after, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: a jet is a kind of aeroplane
S is the abbreviation for section
to book someone is to charge or arrest them

explanation.surface: A police officer makes an arrest in a section of an aircraft with cracked panels.
explanation.walkthrough: JE(S)T is followed by BOOK. The cracks are not fractures but wisecracks, which is why the clue ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A jestbook is a collection of jokes, and a crack is a slangy word for a joke or quip.

clue.text: Chap Maria takes in for tea once in the US?

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside, so one word ends up enclosing another

blocks.note: the name taken as written is the outer shell, giving no letters to the answer

blocks.clueFragment: for tea once in the US
blocks.note: tea was old American slang for marijuana, which is the name Maria with these four letters inside

explanation.surface: A man that Maria brings home for a cup of tea, in an American setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer is what Maria must take in to become the drug. Tea was 1930s American slang for marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan is a common Spanish given name for a man, so it stands for a fellow or bloke.

clue.text: Hybrid cattle in middle of penned part of field

indicators.note: the middle is what remains when the two ends are trimmed off
placing something in another word means setting it inside

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
a dzo is a cross between a yak and a domestic cow

explanation.surface: Crossbred cattle are kept in the middle of a fenced-off part of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes it a farm field, but the field is an American football field. A dzo is a yak-cow cross, a favourite of barred-grid setters.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football the end zone is the scoring area at each end of the playing field.

clue.text: Mostly keeping evergreen

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: saving is keeping something back

explanation.surface: Something that mostly keeps its leaves all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of SAVING. 'Evergreen' looks like an adjective but is used as a noun for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Savin is a species of juniper, a coniferous shrub that keeps its foliage through winter.

clue.text: Migrating sandpiper and type of penguin, not European

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to remove the letter that stands for European

blocks.note: the Terek sandpiper is a wading bird
E is the abbreviation for European, the letter removed
the king penguin is a large species

explanation.surface: Birds on the move: a sandpiper and a penguin that are not from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Terek sandpiper is named after a river in the Caucasus. The birds suggest a migratory species, but the definition is a plain verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekking is making a long, arduous journey, as migrating people or herds do over great distances.

clue.text: German policy, it’s OK perhaps about most of constitution

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered
about means around, so one piece goes round the other
most of means nearly all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
a polity is a form of government or constitution

explanation.surface: A German policy is judged acceptable in relation to most of the constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split around the shortened constitution word. 'It's OK' reads as a verdict, but its letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostpolitik was West Germany's policy of normalising relations with Eastern Europe, pursued by Willy Brandt.

clue.text: Length to which eastern khan might go?

indicators.note: things that go are set in motion and scattered, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written

explanation.surface: How far an Eastern ruler might be willing to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the lengths one will go to' disguises a unit of measurement as a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaneh is an ancient Hebrew unit of measurement equal to six cubits, so it is a measure of distance.

clue.text: James and Penny Stone

blocks.note: Jas is the traditional written abbreviation of James
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: It reads like a couple called James and Penny Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone looks like a surname, but it is the definition. 'Jas' is how James was often abbreviated in old letters and records.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasp is an old form of jasper, an opaque coloured quartz used as a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Going round all of Scotland and southwest Ireland

blocks.note: a' is the Scots form of all
the compass abbreviation
IRL is the international code for Ireland

explanation.surface: A tour that takes in all of Scotland and the southwest of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All of Scotland' looks like the whole country, but it means the Scots word for all, written a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aswirl is in a swirling state, whirling or spinning in circles.

clue.text: Whale’s member — which is a rare shock

blocks.note: the sei is a species of rorqual, plus the possessive s
M is the abbreviation for member

explanation.surface: A whale's member, which is said to be a rare and shocking sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' here means the word itself is rarely used. The sei whale is a familiar crossword creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A seism is an uncommon word for an earthquake, the jolting tremor of the ground.

clue.text: Festival of faithful god for instance tops your year

indicators.note: in a down entry, to top something is to sit above it, so these pieces come first

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
e.g. is the abbreviation for for instance
yr is an abbreviation for your
y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A religious festival where an example deity crowns your year.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the god and the example sit on top of the abbreviations for your and year; 'faithful' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyry is a religious festival or assembly honouring a saint, held by believers.

clue.text: What was unexpected losing wicket in one

definitions.note: phrase used adjectivally: consisting of one

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: someone caught unwary is not expecting what happens
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket shock: a wicket falls out of nowhere in a single delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: UNWARY loses its W. The cricket surface makes 'in one' look like taking a wicket in one ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Unary means composed of a single element or operating on a single item, as in mathematics.

clue.text: City in Wales? Worry endlessly about answer

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: to sweat over something is to worry about it
ans is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone in a Welsh city frets endlessly over an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is there because the definition is a plain description, while the wordplay leans on an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales, the country's second largest.

clue.text: Take note when an old game’s gone commercial

indicators.note: something gone has departed, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: to animadvert is to take notice or comment on something
the indefinite article as a single letter, removed
nim is an ancient counting game played by taking objects from piles, removed

explanation.surface: Pay attention: a classic board game has sold out and become a commercial.
explanation.walkthrough: Animadvert is an uncommon verb, usually meaning to criticise, but originally to take notice. Remove the opening article and game from it.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a shortened form of advertisement, a commercial broadcast or printed notice promoting goods.

clue.text: Small blisters unfortunately ache plenty

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are in disorder

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Small blisters that, sadly, hurt a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a believable complaint; the word is a medical term built from Greek, rarely seen outside dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlyctenae is the plural of phlyctena, a medical term for a small vesicle or pustule on skin or eye.

clue.text: Currently batting with no chance of victory

definitions.note: phrase used adjectivally, as in a no-win situation

blocks.note: now means at the present time
the batting side in cricket is said to be in

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is at the crease with the match already lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets a hopeless scene at the wicket; the two words simply join up into the compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every possible outcome is bad, so success is impossible.

clue.text: Remove a character, shifting the one hiding in recess

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters change their order
something hiding is tucked away inside a larger space

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: Delete a character by moving the person hiding in an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a story, but it means a letter. Aphesis is the loss of an unstressed first sound, as in 'squire' from 'esquire'.
explanation.definitionFit: To aphetise a word is to drop its initial unstressed letter or syllable, a linguistic process.

clue.text: Serious types perhaps drift round about king

indicators.note: to turn round is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
about means around, so it surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: a drift is a bank of snow
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Earnest people may drift around a king at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drift' reads as a verb but is a noun for a snowbank. 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example rather than an exact synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonks are studious, often humourless experts obsessed with detail, so they are one kind of serious person.

clue.text: Missing Dutch queen is fine in broadcast message

indicators.note: saying one thing is another means it becomes it, so one letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: a wireless message is one sent by radio
R for Regina, Latin for queen; this letter is replaced
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A Dutch queen goes missing, and a radio broadcast says she is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch here is not Netherlands: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, from Duchess of Fife. So 'missing Dutch' means lacking a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Wifeless means without a wife; the slang 'Dutch' for a wife makes 'missing Dutch' the same idea.

clue.text: Naively describe as stupid?

blocks.note: to call someone something is to describe them that way
owly, like an owl, is a dictionary word meaning dull-witted

explanation.surface: To label someone simple-mindedly as foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The owl is wise in fable but in Chambers 'owly' means stupid, which is the joke behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means inexperienced and immature, so acting callowly is behaving with youthful innocence.

clue.text: Work autumn in more than one year? Tut, years ago

indicators.note: placing something in another means enclosing it

blocks.note: to till is to work the soil
two Ys, each the abbreviation for year
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Farm labour across several autumns, years back, met with disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Years ago' marks the definition as archaic: the word is a Shakespearean exclamation brushing something aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilly-fally was an Elizabethan exclamation of impatient dismissal, like 'nonsense' or 'pooh'.

clue.text: Flowering herb, mostly sage I found in open country

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the end is cut off
things found in a place are inside it

blocks.note: a sage is wise
taken as written
a lea is open grassland or meadow

explanation.surface: A herb that flowers out in the open, mostly sage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage looks like the plant but is the adjective wise; it is the herb surface that misleads. Lea is a poetic word for a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewisia is a genus of North American flowering plants with succulent leaves, named after Meriwether Lewis.

clue.text: Spot for local plant has added interest

blocks.note: a fern is a plant
to tickle someone's fancy is to interest or amuse them

explanation.surface: A good place for a native plant has extra appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a location, but it is a skin mark, and 'for local' says the word is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferntickle is a Scottish and northern dialect word for a freckle, a small brown mark on the skin.

clue.text: Restore gun I have

blocks.note: to gun an engine is to rev it
the contraction I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone owns a firearm and wants it restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' looks like a weapon but is the verb meaning to race an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive something is to bring it back to life or health, which is to restore it.

clue.text: Finally hook fish with line? This will catch them

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the ide is a freshwater fish
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An angler hooks a fish with rod and line, and is told this is how to catch them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to the fish in the wordplay, so the definition leans on the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidel is a dam or weir in a river with nets or traps set in it to catch fish.

clue.text: Stop Dr No’s counterpart?

blocks.note: taken as written
yup, an informal yes, is the opposite of no

explanation.surface: Halt the Bond villain's opposite number.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No is the James Bond villain; swap his no for its opposite and the imagined doctor becomes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up is to stop talking or to cease flowing, as when a speaker forgets their lines.

clue.text: Defective pan with splits

definitions.note: noun phrase describing something that is flawy

blocks.note: first meaning: having faults
second meaning: a vessel full of cracks, a flaw being a crack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a faulty pan, but each part points to the same adjective: a flaw is a defect and also a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawy, an old dictionary word, means full of flaws, where flaw means both a fault and a physical crack.

clue.text: Unreal missing English typeface

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: aerial in a literary sense means insubstantial or imaginary
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An imaginary font without its English character.
explanation.walkthrough: Aerial here is the airy, insubstantial sense, as in Shakespeare's Ariel rather than a radio antenna.
explanation.definitionFit: Arial is a widely used sans-serif font supplied with Microsoft Windows.

clue.text: Organ that is dead in service

definitions.note: phrase used adjectivally: wearing a servant's uniform

blocks.note: the liver is a body organ
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A body organ that dies during an operation or church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests music in a church service, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveried servants wear livery, the distinctive uniform of a household or company that employs them.

clue.text: American hoax letter about king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fraudulent American letter concerning a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' means a letter of the alphabet written out as a word, not a piece of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: In North American ice hockey a deke is a feint that fools a defender, a decoy move.

clue.text: World Chess Federation backed unknown to improve

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters run the other way

blocks.note: FIDE is the French-based acronym of the world chess body
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: The chess federation supports an unknown player hoping to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reads as supported, but it signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify someone is to instruct them so as to improve them morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Not at all old rumour about Welsh?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: noise once meant a rumour or common talk
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: Nothing whatever in an outdated rumour about the Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' flags that noise in its sense of rumour is obsolete, as in Elizabethan English.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowise is an adverb meaning in no way or to no degree, the same as nowhere near.

clue.text: Fish haul in Arbroath eaten by wheeling birds

indicators.note: wheeling means turning about, so the letters run backwards
what is eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: Aves is the zoological class of birds
rug is a Scots word meaning to pull or tug

explanation.surface: Circling gulls snatch the catch of fish landed at a Scottish port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haul' looks like a catch of fish, but it is a verb, and 'in Arbroath' (a Scottish fishing town) tells you to use the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sevruga is a Caspian sturgeon, prized as the source of a well-known caviar.

clue.text: Trick of former Scots government to do no work in the north

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for government

blocks.clueFragment: do no work in the north
blocks.note: laik is a northern English dialect word for to play or be idle

explanation.surface: A trick by the old Scottish government to avoid any work up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former Scots government' reads as one phrase, but 'former Scots' belongs to the definition, marking the word as obsolete Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaik is an old Scots word for a trick or deception, usually met in the plural glaiks.

clue.text: Star zones turning timelessly?

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
the suffix less means without, so the matching abbreviation is taken out

blocks.note: belts are zones or regions, as in the commuter belt
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Constellations rotating through the sky forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests astronomy alongside 'zones' and 'turning', but it is a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleb is a jokey British spelling of celeb, a celebrity, so a star in the showbusiness sense.

clue.text: Ruffled a pet lyre bird’s feathery parts

indicators.note: ruffled means disordered, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ruffles the plumage of a pet lyrebird.
explanation.walkthrough: The lyrebird belongs to the picture, but the 'lyre' is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterylae are the tracts of skin on a bird's body from which the contour feathers grow.
